one_line: Regional drying/bleaching of a takyr drainage hollow between summer 2024 and 2025; the box is 8 pixels of a 13-17 ha brightening; no mark at 0.86 m.
summary: before.png (median of 2024-07-02 to 2024-10-15) shows the yellow box on mid-toned mottled ground at the southern tip of a dark, finger-like tongue that trails from a drainage line to the north-east, with a bright pan about 300 m to the west; in after.png (2025-06-29 to 2025-08-31) the tongue has turned pale, a pale lobe runs from the pan through the box to the north-east, and the box interior is indistinguishable from the paler ground around it. difference.png shows the brightening as a dendritic, drainage-following network covering roughly a third of the 1.5 km panel, with the box at the southern edge of one of several large red blobs and near-zero NDVI change at the box; timeseries.png shows the footprint and its ring tracking each other through the whole record, both jumping bright in June 2025 with the footprint only a few hundredths above its ring afterwards and greener than it in 2026. hires.png (Esri WorldView-3, 2025-09-10, 0.86 m, three months after first detection) shows only mottled pale pan floor with scattered shrub clumps inside the box, no track, pad, pit, spoil, scorch or object, and wayback_strip.png shows the same tongue-and-pan setting in every release from 2014 to 2026. All three sceptics refuted the candidate: in fresh same-scene composites the footprint's change (+0.046 brightness, +0.043 NBR, +0.003 NDVI) matches its 60-120 m ring to within about 0.005, the adjacent dark tongue changed more than the footprint (NBR -0.086 to +0.018), and the connected region brightening the same way measures 13-17 ha against a 0.32 ha footprint. The pipeline's 'isolated, 0.1%' crowding figure is computed on the step-test mask (optical_change._blobs), not on the raw change field, so it missed a neighbourhood-wide surface-state shift; the detection is a statistical sliver of a regional change, not a discrete mark.
explanation: Interannual surface-state change of a shallow takyr/sor drainage hollow on the Ustyurt plain: a dark, moist floor in the wetter 2024 season bleached to a pale crust in the drier 2025 season, together with the drainage-following network of low ground across the surrounding square kilometre. The 8-pixel footprint is the piece of that regional brightening whose history was quiet enough to pass the step test; the 2025-09-10 0.86 m image shows no disturbance at it.
next_step: Recompute the widespread-change/crowding test on the raw per-pixel 2024-to-2025 brightness and NBR difference at 10 m (connected region touching the footprint, expected 13-17 ha) and feed that into the pipeline; optionally a March-June 2025 per-scene Sentinel-2 MNDWI/SWIR series over the dark tongue to show the floor stood wet before bleaching. No further imagery of the footprint is needed: the 2025-09-10 WorldView-3 view already shows no mark.
